title: BCL Industries Ltd-$ - 524332 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: BCL Industries Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR695 crore with EBITDA margin 9.5%; Bathinda 200 KLPD fire-hit unit restored, full 900 KLPD now running.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was INR695 crore and H1 was INR1,319 crore, with Q2 EBITDA of INR66 crore (9.5% margin) and PAT of INR29 crore (4.2% margin). H1 EBITDA rose 5.9% YoY to INR132 crore, with margin up 191 bps to 10%. The 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol unit, shut after a 19 June fire, resumed on 28 August, restoring the full 900 KLPD distillery capacity. Management flagged that raw material (maize, FCI rice) cost inflation will pressure ethanol margins for the year, though ENA and industrial alcohol prices have been passed through.

financial_highlights.value: INR2 crore from sale of former oil/vanaspati unit assets at Bathinda

segments.name: Distillery (ethanol/ENA)
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA margin 11.9% vs 11% last year, despite higher maize prices. Full 900 KLPD now operational: 550 KLPD Sangat (Punjab) and 350 KLPD Svaksha (West Bengal).

segments.name: Oil refinery
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR188 crore at 3.7% EBITDA margin. Refocused on soft oil refining at 400 TPD each in Bathinda and Kharagpur after exiting packaged oil.

segments.name: PML (country liquor/IMIL)
segments.commentary: Sold 6.42 lakh cases in Q2, up 41.4% YoY. Management says BCL is now the second-largest country liquor player in Punjab.

guidance_outlook: ESY 2025-26 ethanol order book rose 41% to 1.5 lakh KL after an extra 4.37 crore litre allocation for Q4 (2.35 crore litres Sangat, 2.02 crore Svaksha); deliveries continue into November.
Management expects ESY allocations for the new year to be broadly similar to last year.
Margins expected under pressure for the year as maize and FCI rice costs rise; grain distilleries bear most of the burden.
Insurance claim for the Bathinda fire filed; receipt expected by end of Q3 FY27. Amount not disclosed.

CBG: 20 TPD plant planned at Fatehabad; expected revenue about INR70 crore at 90-95% utilisation with 40-45% EBITDA margin. Tender to be floated after Diwali; remaining permissions expected in about 3 months.
Malt plant in Bathinda for IMFL: no application filed yet in Punjab; to be filed after elections. IMFL launch now guided to FY28-29.
Goyal Distillery: environmental clearance for ENA plus ethanol plant applied last month; at least 9-10 months expected.
Dividend payout unlikely to rise in coming years; surplus cash to be reinvested. Debt reduction to follow repayment schedule; working capital utilisation declining.
Management put peak company revenue at INR2,900 crore with added capacity, described as a peak rather than a forecast.
capex_capacity: Total distillery capacity 900 KLPD fully operational after Bathinda 200 KLPD unit resumed on 28 August 2026.
Up to 200 KLPD at each facility can switch between ENA and ethanol; 350 KLPD Bathinda and 150 KLPD Kharagpur are dedicated to ethanol.
CBG plant (20 TPD, Fatehabad) planned; tender after Diwali. Malt plant (Bathinda) and Goyal Distillery expansion (ENA plus ethanol) pending approvals.
Land bank nearly exhausted: about INR10 crore of plots left, apartments sold out; oil mill land expected to be monetised in about a year.
demand_pricing: ENA prices around INR68-70/litre in Q2 vs INR58 in Q1; peak demand season expected for the next 2-3 months.
Maize prices cited at INR29-30 (analyst had estimated INR24-25); ethanol-from-maize realisation cited at about INR68. Management says viability is hampered but still positive.
DDGS prices up slightly; ENA up more.
Biodiesel at INR95/litre in OMC tender judged not viable; refinery margins described as good.
Denatured spirit sales about 15 lakh litres in the current month; no forward contracts due to grain price volatility.
Analyst noted imports of denatured alcohol fell about 99% YoY in July-August; management confirmed demand is good.
Sugar mills diverting less ethanol to ENA; OMC allocations not expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: What allocation and margin outlook for the new ethanol tender year, given rule changes and rate revisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Allocations expected similar to last year; margins under pressure as grain distilleries carry most of the raw material burden. Flexibility to pass costs through in ENA and industrial alcohol.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk of a blending shortfall after the tender changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see the blending target at risk given industry overcapacity, but says it is now survival of the fittest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CBG plant be stand-alone or tied up with OMCs/CGDs?
qa_highlights.answer: Talks with CGDs for LOI on long-term offtake; several EOIs received, too early to comment. Will start with one plant, then plan more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash deployment plan for the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not become a higher-dividend company; cash to go into CBG, malt/IMFL and Goyal Distillery expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential at 900 KLPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak company revenue with added capacity would be INR2,900 crore, a peak and not a forecast; it depends on oil and ENA prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Goyal Distillery and CBG approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal ENA plus ethanol environmental clearance needs 9-10 months; CBG remaining clearances expected in about 3 months; malt application only after Punjab elections.

risks_watch: Grain cost inflation (maize at INR29-30) compressing ethanol margins; the company's ability to pass costs through depends on ENA and industrial alcohol demand.
New ESY tender conditions (sugarcane juice and damaged grain exclusions, rice rules) and uncertainty over Q1 FY28 allocations.
Amount and timing of the Bathinda fire insurance claim (expected by end-Q3 FY27).
Dependence on approvals for Goyal Distillery (9-10 months) and the malt plant (post-elections).
Refinery margin (3.7% in Q2) and the lower-margin oil segment.
Working capital and debt reduction pace; limited land bank left for monetisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations (full capacity restored, PML growth) but cautious on the ethanol sector, with management openly saying margins will be stressed. Evasive on the insurance claim amount and IMFL timing, and reluctant to quantify peak revenue.
key_quotes: So to be completely frank and honest with you, I don't think we'll become a higher-paying dividend company in the coming years.

So I think margins will come under pressure, but thanks to our company's flexibility, especially when it comes to industrial alcohol and ENA, we're able to pass on the costs at least in the ENA and industrial alcohol business.
It's definitely hampered, but I think there's still viability, so we'll continue to do that.
I think peak revenue for our company with this added capacity will be INR2,900 crores, not more.

adds.what: 20 TPD CBG plant at Fatehabad (revenue ~INR70 crore at 90-95% utilisation)
Goyal Distillery ENA plus ethanol expansion (pending environmental clearance, 9-10 months)
Malt plant in Bathinda for IMFL (no application filed; IMFL launch guided FY28-29)

growth.why: Management guides peak company revenue of INR2,900 crore with added capacity (explicitly a peak, not a forecast) and says margins will be under pressure from maize and FCI rice costs; the 900 KLPD distillery is fully running, but the new CBG, Goyal and malt projects are still pending approvals and tenders with no firm revenue growth percentage guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says margins will be under pressure for the year as maize (INR29-30 vs analyst's INR24-25) and FCI rice costs rise, with grain distilleries bearing most of the burden, though Q2 distillery margin still rose to 11.9% from 11%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CBG 20 TPD plant at Fatehabad needs remaining permissions in about 3 months with tender after Diwali; Goyal Distillery ENA plus ethanol needs 9-10 months of environmental clearance, so new capacity lands only beyond the window, while the 900 KLPD distillery is already fully running.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 ENA volume rose to 22,500 KL from 12,130 KL YoY with the full 900 KLPD back online after the 28 August restart, PML cases up 41.4% YoY to 6.42 lakh, and ESY 2025-26 order book up 41% to 1.5 lakh KL; but ENA peak season is only 2-3 months and new ESY allocations are expected broadly similar.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is redirecting surplus cash into CBG, malt/IMFL and Goyal expansion with CBG tender after Diwali and approvals pending, though distillery utilisation is now at full 900 KLPD and land bank is nearly exhausted (about INR10 crore left).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise was given; management explicitly flagged ethanol margin pressure and called the INR2,900 crore peak revenue a peak, not a forecast.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Grain cost inflation (maize at INR29-30) is compressing ethanol margins and new ESY tender conditions and Q1 FY28 allocation uncertainty could weigh; refinery margin is only 3.7% and the Bathinda insurance claim amount is undisclosed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: IMFL launch is now guided to FY28-29 with the malt plant application not yet filed until after Punjab elections; CBG and Goyal are capacity additions, not product launches in the window.

rows.label: Bathinda fire insurance claim receipt
rows.why: Claim filed and receipt expected by end of Q3 FY27, with the amount not disclosed, so it could give a one-time cash and other income boost.

rows.label: CBG offtake LOI with CGDs/OMCs
rows.why: Talks with CGDs for long-term offtake LOI are underway with several EOIs received, but management says it is too early to comment and it will start with one plant.

rows.label: Debt reduction and lower working capital
rows.why: Management says debt reduction will follow the repayment schedule and working capital utilisation is declining, with surplus cash reinvested rather than paid out as dividends.

tone.note: Management was confident on restored 900 KLPD operations and PML growth but cautious on ethanol margins from grain cost inflation; analysts pushed on tender-year allocations, blending risk, CBG offtake and peak revenue, which management declined to quantify.
